known_issue_discovered_and_fixed_this_se: During policy setup, add_approver/seal_policy calls made through genlayer_py's write_contract() with a raw address string silently reverted on-chain (AttributeError inside the contract's storage layer) despite the transaction reporting FINALIZED/MAJORITY_AGREE at the top level -- validators were agreeing on the ERROR outcome, not a success. Root cause: Address-typed contract arguments must be explicitly wrapped (genlayer_py.types.CalldataAddress) when submitted via the Python SDK; a raw hex string is not auto-converted. Confirmed via `genlayer receipt <hash>` showing the leader's Python traceback. Fixed in the calling script; not a contract bug. The 8 transaction hashes below under pre_fix_reverted_attempts are the real, on-chain reverted attempts from before this fix.

historical_pre_fix_deployment.note: Superseded. This was the deployment of the UNFIXED contract source (validator treated leader result as a plain dict instead of unwrapping gl.vm.Return), which caused every assess_action call to be rejected by validators regardless of leader correctness. Kept here only as historical evidence for the root-cause narrative in BUILD_STATUS.md.
historical_pre_fix_deployment.corrected_root_cause: The validator function indexed the leader result as a plain dict; on live GenVM the leader result is wrapped in gl.vm.Return with the payload in .calldata. This meant validate() either crashed or always compared against garbage, so it rejected every leader proposal regardless of correctness. The cross-model-heterogeneity explanation recorded at the time was incorrect and is superseded by this finding. After fixing validate() to unwrap gl.vm.Return, the same class of action reached real substantive MAJORITY_AGREE consensus on the first attempt every time in this session (see live_lifecycle_cases above).
